data.name: Heading
data.comment: The heading of the Frame panel: the video's picture area, its shape and how the photos fill it (as a picture frame), not one picture of the video. Keep it to about 14 characters: it is also a tab in a narrow window, beside Timing and Output.

data.name: ShapeName
data.comment: The screen reader name of the row that picks the video's shape (Match, 16:9, 9:16, 1:1, 4:5, 4:3): its aspect ratio.

data.name: FitName
data.comment: The screen reader name of the two-part switch that picks Fit or Fill: how a photo of another shape is placed in the frame. A noun for that choice ("Fit" as in "fit to frame"), not the option FitOption.

data.name: ShapeMatch
data.comment: The first shape, as its segment shows it: take the shape of the photos themselves. Keep it to about 6 characters: six equal segments share the 280 px row (about 46 px each), and a longer word ends in an ellipsis (its screen reader name is ShapeMatchName).

data.name: ShapeMatchName
data.comment: The first shape as a screen reader names it, and in sentences: the video takes the photos' shape.

data.name: FitOption
data.comment: The first part of the Fit or Fill switch: show the whole photo, with bars where its shape differs from the frame's. A verb or short noun. Keep it to about 12 characters: the two parts share the 280 px row.

data.name: FillOption
data.comment: The second part of the Fit or Fill switch: fill the frame and cut the photo's edges. Keep it to about 12 characters.

data.name: FitHint
data.value: {0} shows the whole photo with bars where shapes differ.
data.comment: The line under the switches when Fit is chosen. {0} the option's label, FitOption ("Fit"), so the line always matches the switch.

data.name: FillHint
data.value: {0} crops the edges so the frame has no bars.
data.comment: The line under the switches when Fill is chosen. {0} the option's label, FillOption ("Fill"), so the line always matches the switch.

data.name: MatchingPhotos
data.comment: The line under the switches when Match photos is chosen and the photos' sizes are known. {0} the width, {1} the height of the most common photo, in pixels ("4032", "3024", written without grouping).

data.name: MatchingNoPhotos
data.value: Matching your photos. Until their sizes are known the shape is 16:9.
data.comment: The same line when no photo size is known yet (no photos, or none read), so the video is 16:9.

data.name: NoSize
data.value: Photos this wide or tall are too large to export on this PC. Pick a fixed shape such as 16:9.
data.comment: The line when Match photos gives a shape so wide or tall that no size can be exported on this PC; says what to do instead.

data.name: PortraitHint
data.value: Most of your photos are portrait, so 9:16 suits them better.
data.comment: A quiet suggestion when most photos are portrait (taller than wide) and the shape is landscape.

data.name: PortraitApply
data.comment: The suggestion's button that switches to 9:16. Keep it to about 14 characters.

data.name: PortraitDismiss
data.comment: The suggestion's button that hides it for this project. Keep it to about 14 characters.

data.name: Announcement
data.comment: Read by a screen reader after a change in the Frame panel ("Frame: 16:9, Fit."). {0} the panel's heading, Heading ("Frame"), {1} the shape's name ("16:9", "Match photos"), {2} FitOption or FillOption. Adjust the punctuation to your language's rules.
